title: Adu and the Catch That Took a Team

pages.text: At break time, Dery threw a ball to Adu. Adu saw it coming, ran two steps and caught it. “Great catch!” said Dery. “How did you do that so fast?”
sentences: At break time, Dery threw a ball to Adu.
Adu saw it coming, ran two steps and caught it.
“Great catch!” said Dery.
“How did you do that so fast?”
pages.alt: In a sunny Ghanaian schoolyard at break time, Adu leaps two steps forward and catches a ball cleanly in both hands while Dery cheers.

pages.text: Their teacher came over. “Let us slow it down,” she said. “First, your eyes saw the ball. Your eyes are sense organs. They tell you what is happening around you.”
sentences: Their teacher came over.
“Let us slow it down,” she said.
“First, your eyes saw the ball.
Your eyes are sense organs.
They tell you what is happening around you.”
pages.alt: Their smiling teacher kneels slightly in the schoolyard and gestures gently near her own eyes while Adu holds the ball and Dery listens.

pages.text: “Next, your brain,” said the teacher. “Your brain is in your head. It got the message from your eyes and decided what to do. Then it sent a message to your legs and hands.”
sentences: “Next, your brain,” said the teacher.
“Your brain is in your head.
It got the message from your eyes and decided what to do.
Then it sent a message to your legs and hands.”
pages.alt: Under the shade of a school veranda, the teacher taps the side of her head gently to indicate thinking while Adu and Dery point thoughtfully to their heads, hands and legs.

pages.text: “Your legs moved you to the right place,” she said. “Your hands closed around the ball. Your bones and muscles helped you move. Your body parts work together like a team.”
sentences: “Your legs moved you to the right place,” she said.
“Your hands closed around the ball.
Your bones and muscles helped you move.
Your body parts work together like a team.”
pages.alt: Adu demonstrates running swiftly on strong legs with his hands curved ready to catch the ball while Dery and the teacher watch.

pages.text: “And your heart pumped blood to all those parts,” she added. “Your breath gave you air. That is why you feel warm and breathe fast after a game.” Dery put a hand on her chest. “I can feel it.”
sentences: “And your heart pumped blood to all those parts,” she added.
“Your breath gave you air.
That is why you feel warm and breathe fast after a game.” Dery put a hand on her chest.
“I can feel it.”
pages.alt: Standing in the sunlit courtyard after playing, Dery places her hand gently over her chest to feel her heartbeat while Adu smiles beside her.

pages.text: The children played again. This time, Dery caught the ball. “My team worked!” she laughed. “And when we eat well, drink water and rest, the team stays strong.”
sentences: The children played again.
This time, Dery caught the ball.
“My team worked!” she laughed.
“And when we eat well, drink water and rest, the team stays strong.”
pages.alt: Dery catches the ball joyfully in both hands in the sunny schoolyard while Adu claps and a clean water bottle sits on a bench nearby.

activities.question: Which body part sent a message to Adu’s legs and hands?
What helps the body team stay strong?
options: Eating well, drinking water and resting

items: The brain decides what to do.

activities.definition: Parts of the body that help bones move.

glossary.definition: The part of the body in the head that thinks and sends messages.
Parts of the body that help bones move.
